property_summary: After a Collect call, the value of MinSum remains the same as before the call.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), the value of MinSum must equal the argument passed to the last SetMinSum call.
After calling SetMinSum with a value, then calling Collect, MinSum should equal the value passed to SetMinSum (not 0).
After any number of calls, the MinSum value is always equal to the value last passed to SetMinSum if it was called, otherwise it remains zero.
After Initialized() is called, the MinSum value remains the same before and after any Collect call.
The value of MinSum should never change after any call to Collect.
The value of MinSum remains unchanged after any sequence of calls ending with Collect.
After any call to Collect, the value of MinSum equals its value after the previous public call, i.e., MinSum is never changed by Collect.
After any call to Collect, MinSum is unchanged from its previous value.
After any call to Collect, the value of MinSum is unchanged (i.e., remains equal to its value immediately before the Collect call).
The value of SetMinSum is never changed after Initialized is called, regardless of any calls to other functions.
After Initialized is called, calling Collect (which may or may not succeed) never changes SetMinSum.
After Initialized is called, SetMinSum remains unchanged regardless of the arguments to Collect.
After Initialized() is called, SetMinSum() retains its value regardless of calls to other functions, including Collect().
State variable Log always points to a contract of type LogFile after SetLogFile is called.
After SetLogFile is called, the MinSum state variable remains unchanged by subsequent Collect calls.
After calling SetLogFile and then Collect, the value of SetLogFile (which is a LogFile address in the original) is always non-zero when MinSum is non-zero.
After SetLogFile is called, subsequent Collect calls never change the MinSum state variable.
After SetLogFile is called, subsequent Collect calls do not change the Log state variable.
After a successful Collect call, the Log address must equal the address set by SetLogFile.
After a Collect call, the Log address returned by the public getter SetLogFile is unchanged from its previous value.
After Collect, the LogFile address is always the same as before the call.
After any call to Collect, the public getter SetLogFile returns a non-zero address.
After a Collect call, the LogFile address is non-zero if a SetLogFile call was made before initialization.
The total balance of the contract after Collect only decreases by the amount transferred, regardless of initialization state.
The value of SetLogFile state variable after a Collect call is always the same as before the call.
The value returned by SetLogFile() after a Collect call equals the initial value set in setUp().
After any Collect call, the address returned by SetLogFile() remains unchanged from its initial value set in setUp().
The value of SetLogFile() remains unchanged before and after any Collect call, regardless of inputs.
After a Collect call, the address in Log cannot be changed — SetLogFile() must remain the same regardless of inputs.
SetLogFile always returns the same address regardless of how many times Collect is called with any fuzz parameters.
After Collect is called, the LogFile address remains the address set during initialization, which is the zero address because SetLogFile was never called in setUp.

After a call to Collect, the state variable SetLogFile remains equal to the last address explicitly set by a call to SetLogFile (including the initial default zero address), regardless of the fuzz inputs.
After a Collect call, SetLogFile() returns the same address as before the Collect call, for any valid fuzz inputs.
After depositing and then calling Collect with a non-zero amount, the contract's balance decreases by exactly the collected amount.
When Collect succeeds, the contract's Ether balance decreases exactly by the amount collected.
After a call to Collect, the total balance stored in the Acc mapping plus the contract's Ether balance is invariant with respect to the amount transferred out.
After any sequence of operations ending with a Collect call, the sender's stored balance does not increase beyond its initial value plus deposited ETH.
After any call to Collect, the msg.sender's stored balance in the Acc mapping is unchanged from before the call.
The Collect function should not transfer funds when the requested amount exceeds the account balance.
After a Collect call, the contract's ether balance should never increase.
After a successful Collect call (one that does not revert), the contract's total ether balance (address(c).balance) should not increase.
After any Collect call, the contract's balance (address(c).balance) must be at most the sum of all account balances recorded in Acc, plus the contract's initial balance (which is 0).
After Collect, the sum of all Acc balances plus the contract balance must be invariant (equal to contract's initial balance if no external funds added).
